subject: physics
question_text: State the laws of static friction and the laws of kinetic friction.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Laws of static friction
lines: 1) Static friction adjusts itself to equal
the applied force, up to a maximum value.
2) That maximum, the limiting friction, is
proportional to the normal force: f_s = μ_s N.
3) It does not depend on the area of contact.
steps.why: The first law is the one students miss: below the limit, friction is not μ_s N at all — it is whatever the push happens to be.
common_mistakes: Writing f_s = μ_s N for every case; that is only the MAXIMUM value.

recall.must_convey: That static friction adjusts up to a maximum, the maximum is mu s N, and it does not depend on the area of contact.
accept: adjusts itself up to a maximum
independent of the area of contact
reject: f k equals mu k N

steps.label: Laws of kinetic friction
lines: 1) Kinetic friction is proportional to the
2) It does not depend on the area of contact
or, over ordinary speeds, on the speed.

lines.text: μ_k is always less than μ_s

steps.why: Kinetic friction has a fixed value while static friction has a range — that single difference explains why a sliding load is easier to move than a stationary one.
common_mistakes: Saying kinetic friction grows with speed; over ordinary speeds it does not.

recall.must_convey: That kinetic friction is mu k N, independent of area and of speed, and mu k is less than mu s.
accept: f k equals mu k N
mu k is less than mu s
reject: adjusts itself up to a maximum
